instruction.text: Read the poem and identify syntactical devices.

atoms.text:
Streets that whisper, walls that weep, windows that watch—
all bear witness to the
endless, restless, breathless rhythm.

Here the rich reside,
here the poor persist,
here the hopeful hurry
toward horizons painted with possibility.

Time here moves like molasses in July,
thick and sweet
and suffocating.

atoms.text:
The leaves are falling, falling
through the crisp October air
—red, gold, bronze, copper—
scattered across the ground
where children gather them in baskets.

They are falling, falling
from branches stripped bare by wind
and time and seasons turning.
Birds, squirrels, insects
seek their shelter before winter comes.

Still falling, falling,
the leaves descend like memories
we cannot hold, like moments
slipping through our hands.
